items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: The same as like Caruso would get.

ctx.x: I forgot certain incidents at places like we played in London before we came back to America. We were asked by the British government to play at the Savoy Hotel. That was a celebration of the Peace Victory Ball. Yeah we worked to play the dance music and we went on over there after they had all the parades and all kinds of ceremonies in the street all day. People were kissing one another. Men were even kissing you on the street. They were so happy. That night we went over to the Savoy Hotel and we mounted the…

Yes that's right. We'll keep it now. This is a letter from Emil Christian and it says I would like Philip Napoleon on cornet and Johnny Costello on clarinet. The boys I was working with because they have more of an idea what I want and they can play all the Dixieland numbers because I'll know we'll get some requests for them. It's signed on the back here. items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: I played on the bills with Caruso.

ctx.x: And did Columbia issue those records? That's another question.

They didn't issue them till May, till the Liber Stable Blues became a national hit. It was all over the world, even down in Honolulu. And all the way the American forces went, they were carried overseas by the American troops, which we entertained over a million men. I had pastors to every fort and every hospital in New York.
